This passage — categorized here as exposition quoting scripture — highlights Bahá’u’lláh's teaching that the return of past Revelations and their central figures is an established reality in each new dispensation.

To give you the exact location and translation details for the *Íqán*'s discussion of Elijah and John the Baptist, you would want to look directly at Shoghi Effendi's English translation of the *Kitáb-i-Íqán* (published by the Bahá'í Publishing Trust), where Bahá'u'lláh treats the Gospel questions surrounding John's identity at length in the early sections of the book.

In that last quotation you give the phrase "exactly like (ayn be ayn)" — can you explain what 'ayn' means in that construction, and whether Bahá'u'lláh uses it elsewhere to describe the relation between Prophets, since it seems to be a different claim from a simple 'return' (raj'a)?

The term you are looking at is the Arabic word *‘ayn* (عین), which literally means an eye, a fountain or spring, or the essence and very self of a thing. As the passages use it—and as Bahá’u’lláh explains the deeper meaning of “return” (*raj‘a*)—it points not to physical reincarnation, but to the identity of divine station and attributes.

In *The Kitáb-i-Íqán*, Bahá’u’lláh describes how the companions and followers of a new Manifestation are considered the "return" of those from a former Dispensation, existing "in name, in reality, in deeds, in words, and in rank" ([*The Kitáb-i-Íqán*](https://oceanlibrary.com/kitab-i-iqan_bahaullah/?paraId=para_181&selectionString=kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_7t.0~kitab-i-iqan-prod-version_en_7t.646)). Similarly, when speaking of the unity of the Prophets themselves, Bahá’u’lláh writes:

> It is clear and evident to thee that all the Prophets are the Temples of the Cause of God, Who have appeared clothed in divers attire. If thou wilt observe with discriminating eyes, thou wilt behold Them all abiding in the same tabernacle, soaring in the same heaven, seated upon the same throne, uttering the same speech, and proclaiming the same Faith. — *Gleanings from the Writings of Bahá’u’lláh*

In authorized interpretation, Shoghi Effendi explains that such an identification means a Manifestation or holy soul identifies "His Spirit with these Holy Souls gone before; that does not, of course, make Him in any way their reincarnation" ([*Lights of Guidance*](https://oceanoflights.org/lights-of-guidance-baha-i-ocean-en/#:~:text=In%20the%20prayer%20mentioned,%7Bid%3D%22para6324%22%20ilmid%3D%22bl44a%22%20type%3D%22par%22%20language%3D%22en%22%7D) — quoted in a work by Helen Hornby).

You say the Íqán describes followers as the "return" of earlier ones "in name, in reality, in deeds, in words, and in rank"; how does that compare with the Shoghi Effendi statement from *Lights of Guidance* that a Manifestation is "in no way their reincarnation," and with the Augustine/Plato material on resurrection you cited earlier?

Hello, friend,
